findings.reason: from_events.ts:153-155 reads state.frames[length-1] and then frame.kind with no check, because the diff removed the 'node appears outside a document' throw. A node event with no open frame now hits a TypeError. eventsToAst is public (index.ts:193), while constructor.ts:319 still guards this case.
findings.claim: A node event with no open frame now crashes with a raw TypeError instead of a positioned parser error.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `if (!frame) throwErrorAt(state.parserState, state.position, 'node appears outside a document')`. Line 155 now reads `frame.kind` directly on `state.frames[state.frames.length - 1]`, which is undefined when the frame stack is empty. eventsToAst is exported publicly (src/index.ts:193), so callers can pass any ParserState. The sibling walker in src/parser/constructor.ts:321 still keeps this check.

findings.reason: from_events.ts:230 is now `state.frames.pop()!`, and the next line reads frame.kind. An extra EVENT_POP therefore throws an unpositioned TypeError where it used to throw 'unexpected collection end'. constructor.ts:438 keeps the check.
findings.claim: An unbalanced EVENT_POP is no longer reported; the non-null assertion only silences TypeScript.
findings.evidence: The diff swaps `const frame = state.frames.pop(); if (!frame) throwErrorAt(parserState, state.position, 'unexpected collection end')` for `const frame = state.frames.pop()!`. The `!` only silences TypeScript and does nothing at runtime. src/parser/constructor.ts:439 keeps the equivalent check.

findings.reason: The diff deletes the final frames.length check, and the function now returns state.stream directly. A document only reaches the stream on its EVENT_POP, so in a truncated stream the unfinished documents are silently dropped. constructor.ts:456 still throws on this. Both reviewers found it; I kept severity high.
findings.claim: A truncated event stream with open frames silently returns a partial Stream instead of erroring.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `if (state.frames.length !== 0) throwErrorAt(parserState, state.position, 'unexpected end of event stream')`. The function now ends with a bare `return state.stream`, and documents only reach the stream when their EVENT_POP arrives (line 232). src/parser/constructor.ts:456 keeps this check, so the two walkers now behave differently on the same input.

findings.reason: NO_RANGE is -1 (from_events.ts:39), and slice(-1,-1) returns '', so behavior is unchanged when both ends are unset. The parser sets anchorStart and anchorEnd together (parser.ts:237-238), so the mixed case the finding relies on doesn't come up. This is a readability point, not a defect.
findings.claim: Removing the NO_RANGE guard on alias names relies on slice(-1,-1) returning ''.
findings.evidence: The diff replaces `event.anchorStart === NO_RANGE ? '' : parserState.input.slice(...)` with an unconditional `parserState.input.slice(event.anchorStart, event.anchorEnd)`. Negative slice indexes count from the end of the input. constructor.ts:426-428 and anchorName() in this same file (line 89) both keep the guard.
